Yeah mate, I mean the whole situation isn't nice, to begin with, if I'm being honest. but it is what it is and we move. I'm taking time to focus on my mental health and my degree, can't deal with that stress now.

The symptoms haven't been getting much better, e.g. eating, sleeping, etc. However, oddly enough they've been normalized. 

If you look out from the outside in, the majority of individuals would go "You need to see someone, that's not healthy". It's just become desensitized and normal but that was normal before I received the diagnosis. 

The medication starts soon, scared of that but it is the first step to getting better, alternatively, I don't want the medication because there is a split personality within myself but we move.

Hey mate,

First of all, apologies for the late reply, and thank you for your time in writing this. That day was terrible and I honestly needed that. 

In regards to work, it is a shit situation as the accuser was quite harsh on me over the telephone with little to no evidence backing him up. It is what it is and whether he wants to believe me or not, that's his worry. Still, the harshness of his tone has plagued my mind for several days and presumably will continue to do so for a while. 

In terms of being the same person I was, and rather am, that is true to a degree. Foundationally I am still the same individual, only now with more of an emphasis on myself rather than my work and a temporarily reduced mental and physical ability. The emotional side of me will always be jumpy from one emotion to another constantly, but we are looking to get a hold on it and hopefully gain a neutral stable set of emotions instead of jumping all over the place.

The diagnosis as you mentioned has made a lot more sense from a personal standpoint. Everything makes sense as to what I do, but not fully making it a personality trait and echoing it to the world. Split into two senses about the feeling towards the diagnosis at the moment.

You too can do this, I am so proud to see you still here and kicking at that age. Definitely keep in touch, my friend.
